coverLetter:
Priya Raman
Toronto, Canada
priya.raman@example.com
+1 555 0176

October 13, 2026

Hiring Manager
Duolingo

Dear Hiring Manager,

Your ad asks for backend engineers who can build and operate reliable, scalable systems and own hard problems from design through production. At Lumen Payments, a fintech with 300 staff, the payment status API was slow on hot reads. I moved those reads from PostgreSQL to Redis and cut p99 latency from 480 ms to 120 ms. That kind of fix is what I do best.

I'm a backend engineer with 11 years of experience building payment and event-processing services in Kotlin, Java and Python. I designed and ran the settlement service in Kotlin and Spring Boot on Kafka, and I led a team of 4 engineers through a 9 month migration from a monolith to 6 services. I was on call for the payments platform and wrote the post-incident reviews for 14 incidents, so operating systems in production is familiar ground. On AWS (EC2, RDS, SQS, S3) and Datadog, I've built and monitored services, and I earned my AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate in 2024. My B.Sc. in Computer Science from the University of Waterloo covers the fundamentals you list. As the Ads team scales ad serving and works across product, design and data science, I'd bring API design and event-driven architecture experience to that work.

I'm back in full-time engineering after a planned career break and ready to start. I'd welcome a conversation about how I can contribute to the backend team at Duolingo.

Best regards,
Priya Raman

applicationEmail.body:
Hello Duolingo Hiring Team,

I led a team of 4 engineers through a 9 month migration from a monolith to 6 services at Lumen Payments, and I'd like to bring that same mix of backend design and steady shipping to your Backend Engineer II role. My day-to-day work is Kotlin, Java, Python and PostgreSQL, and I've designed, run and been on call for production services. My CV and cover letter are attached for you to look through. I'm available for a call any weekday this week and can start a conversation whenever suits your team.

Best regards,
Priya Raman
